statement.text:
(a) Does every Jordan curve in the Euclidean plane contain the vertices of a
square?
(b) Does every Jordan curve in the Euclidean plane contain the vertices of the
affine image of a regular hexagon?
(c) Let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth Jordan curve, and let $S \subset \mathbb{C}$ consist of $2n \geq 4$
concyclic points. Does there exist a non-constant polynomial $p(z) \in \mathbb{C}[z]$
of degree $< n$ such that $p(S) \subset \gamma$?
(d) Suppose that $h$ is a continuous, real-valued function defined on the unit
sphere $S^{2} \subset \mathbb{R}^{3}$ and that points $x_{1},..., x_{4} \in S^{2}$ form the vertices of
a square.
Is there an isometry $\rho \in \operatorname{SO}(3)$ such that $h$ is constant on
$\rho(x_{1}),..., \rho(x_{4})$?
